_comment: DECLARATIVE FIXTURE for the QA tenant (db/seeds/qa-tenant.ts). This file is
WHAT THE QA TENANT CONTAINS. It is not a description of the QA tenant and it
is not a copy of one — the seed makes the database match this file, so a
reviewer reads the diff and knows exactly what an e2e run drives.
WHY A FIXTURE AND NOT A COPY OF `educar-mais-contexto`: measured 2026-08-13,
the authoring MCP tool `instantiate_program` deep-copies WITHIN ONE TENANT
only (it inserts every row with `tenant_id: srcRow.tenant_id`). There is no
cross-tenant copy primitive, so copying dfl-batch content into `qa-e2e` is
not merely discouraged — it is not possible. That constraint pushed us to
the better answer anyway: a copy would couple QA to whatever production
holds today and would drift the moment an author edits the real cohort's
lesson, silently and with no diff to review.
NATURAL KEYS. `itera.units`, `itera.lessons` and `itera.activities` have no
slug and no unique business key. The seed therefore matches on ORDINAL
within the parent (`units.ordinal` in the program, `lessons.ordinal` in the
unit, `activities.ordinal` in the lesson). Re-ordering entries in this file
REWRITES the existing rows in place rather than creating new ones; that is
deliberate, because the alternative — appending on every run — is exactly
the non-idempotence this seed exists to avoid.

tenant.name: QA — automated test identities
_comment: Created 2026-08-13 by `itera.create_test_tenant` (migration 0066), id
4f7ac88e-cba2-407b-b917-1c5618f1b9b1, `is_test = true`. The seed calls
the same function, which is idempotent by slug, so it also builds the
tenant from nothing. The slug must match `^qa-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` — the
function refuses anything else.

members.why: The seed itself authenticates as this identity. Measured 2026-08-13: it holds `tenant_admin` on `qa-e2e`, which puts the tenant inside `itera.current_author_tenant_ids()` (that function accepts author/instructor/tenant_admin/owner), so it may INSERT programs, units, lessons and activities here. Listed for completeness; the seed never has to grant it.
`ITERA_E2E_PROF_*`. Starts the live class in e2e/live-instructor-routed.spec.ts.
`ITERA_E2E_ALUNO1_*`. Joins the live class, and writes the reflection in e2e/artifact-persistence.spec.ts.
`ITERA_E2E_ALUNO2_*`. The peer whose blindness to aluno1's work is the isolation assertion. Must share a tenant with aluno1 or that assertion proves nothing.

_comment: ONE lesson serves both specs, because both read the SAME env var
(`ITERA_E2E_LESSON_ID`). That forces one lesson to satisfy two
shapes at once:
· e2e/artifact-persistence.spec.ts opens /lesson/:id and expects
`document-reflection-input` to be VISIBLE, so the reflection
must be the FIRST activity — the player opens on ordinal 0;
· e2e/live-instructor-routed.spec.ts only needs the lesson to
hold at least one activity (InstructorClassPage guards Start on
`firstActivityId` being non-null), and something to advance to.
A reflection first is unusual pedagogy and deliberate here.

spec.prompt: Escreva, com suas palavras, o que você espera aprender nesta aula de teste.
spec.body: Esta é uma atividade de QA. Nada escrito aqui é conteúdo pedagógico real.

_comment: `document` + `spec.prompt` + `rubric.min_words` is the REDAÇÃO
contract (src/stories/contractFixtures.ts): the renderer swaps
'mark as done' for a textarea with a word counter, and
`document-reflection-input` appears. Without the prompt/rubric
it renders as reading and that test id never exists.
`min_words: 12` is measured, not chosen. The text
artifact-persistence.spec.ts types is ~17 words. A higher floor
would leave 'activity-done' disabled and the spec would fail on
a fixture defect that looks like a product bug.
`artifact_policy` is left unset ('{}' → mode 'auto'). Under
auto, KIND_ARTIFACT_DEFAULTS persists `document`, which is what
puts `reflection.md` in 'My repository'. Setting it explicitly
would pin behaviour the product owns.

Esta também não é a opção correta

_comment: The second activity the live class can advance to. Shape copied
from a production `single_choice` row read 2026-08-13, so it is
the contract the renderer actually consumes, not one invented
here.
`status: published` on both. An activity defaults to `draft`,
and `activities_select_tenant` only lets a non-author read a
row that is `published`. A draft fixture would be invisible to
aluno1/aluno2 while staying visible to the seed's own identity
— a fixture that looks correct from the only place that can see
it is the worst kind.
